dutch_naturalness.explanation: 'Ik heb een fiets.' is idiomatic, everyday Dutch with 'heb' in the possession sense, parallel to the source examples 'Ik heb een mooi huis.' (nl:56) and 'Ik heb een nieuwe auto.' (pl:469).

en_pl_translation.explanation: EN 'I have a bicycle.' and PL 'Mam rower.' (natural pro-drop, as in pl:469 'Mam nowe auto.') are direct and keep person, number and tense; the meanings render the Dutch anchor faithfully.

task_ambiguity.explanation: In 'Ik ___ een fiets.' the cue 'have; possess or have available' / 'mieć; posiadać lub mieć do dyspozycji' does not fix the tense, so 'had' ('Ik had een fiets.') is a valid answer of the same sense that would be marked wrong. The cue's own word 'possess' / 'posiadać' also invites 'bezit' ('Ik bezit een fiets.'), grammatical and literally what the cue says. A cue naming only the head meaning and the tense removes both (patch).

span_form_contract.explanation: The span [3,6) slices exactly 'heb', and target_form_ids points to the first-person singular present 'heb' (0293e1eb, en:175 /forms/4), which agrees with 'Ik'; it is one segment with no particle or reflexive.
